The helper `roles` is the ONLY place these tests read `Theme` fields, so 8.3b edits one function; the expected arrays are in field order (main_bg, main_text, matching_bg, selected_bg, selected_text, selected_matching_bg, description_text, description_border):

```rust
    /// The eight colours of a theme in field order: main_bg, main_text, matching_bg, selected_bg, selected_text,
    /// selected_matching_bg, description_text, description_border.
    fn roles(t: &Theme) -> [Rgb; 8] {
        [
            t.main_bg,
            t.main_text,
            t.matching_bg,
            t.selected_bg,
            t.selected_text,
            t.selected_matching_bg,
            t.description_text,
            t.description_border,
        ]
    }

    #[test]
    fn should_draw_a_json_value_that_is_not_a_fig_theme_with_the_base16_filler() {
        let filler = [
            (24, 24, 24),
            (232, 232, 232),
            (40, 40, 40),
            (56, 56, 56),
            (248, 248, 248),
            (186, 139, 175),
            (216, 216, 216),
            (40, 40, 40),
        ];
        let not_fig = [
            json!({}),
            json!([1]),
            json!("x"),
            json!(null),
            json!(5),
            json!({"version": "1.0"}),
            json!({"version": 1, "theme": {}}),
            json!({"version": "1.0", "theme": "x"}),
        ];

        for value in not_fig {
            assert_eq!(roles(&Theme::from_json(&value)), filler, "{value}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn should_fall_back_per_colour_for_a_fig_theme_with_missing_or_unparsable_colours() {
        let fig = json!({
            "version": "1.0",
            "theme": {
                "backgroundColor": "#000",
                "matchBackgroundColor": "red",
                "selection": {"backgroundColor": 5, "textColor": null, "matchBackgroundColor": "rgb(1,2)"},
                "description": {"textColor": "#102030"}
            }
        });
        let dark = [
            (48, 48, 48),
            (180, 180, 180),
            (95, 89, 56),
            (30, 90, 199),
            (253, 253, 253),
            (106, 142, 218),
            (180, 180, 180),
            (65, 65, 65),
        ];

        let theme = Theme::from_json(&fig);

        assert_eq!(
            roles(&theme),
            [
                (0, 0, 0),
                dark[1],
                dark[2],
                dark[3],
                dark[4],
                dark[5],
                (16, 32, 48),
                dark[7]
            ]
        );
        // a Fig theme without a single colour is dark, not the base16 filler
        let empty = json!({"version": "1.0", "theme": {}});
        assert_eq!(roles(&Theme::from_json(&empty)), dark);
    }

    #[test]
    fn should_fall_back_per_colour_for_a_base16_theme_with_missing_or_unparsable_colours() {
        let base16 = json!({
            "shade0": "#101010",
            "shade1": "#0a0b0c",
            "shade5": 5,
            "shade6": null,
            "shade7": "red",
            "accent6": "rgb(1,2)",
            "shade3": "#ffffff",
            "accent0": "#ffffff"
        });

        let theme = Theme::from_json(&base16);

        assert_eq!(
            roles(&theme),
            [
                (16, 16, 16),
                (232, 232, 232),
                (10, 11, 12),
                (56, 56, 56),
                (248, 248, 248),
                (186, 139, 175),
                (216, 216, 216),
                (10, 11, 12)
            ]
        );
    }
```

The filler values are `SHADES`/`ACCENTS` (`#181818` ... `#ba8baf`), the dark values are `Theme::dark()`; if a literal of yours disagrees with a run, the run is right: stop and report instead of editing a literal.

## Traps (check each)

BIN="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$1")"
BINDIR="$(dirname "$BIN")"
SANDBOXES=()
cleanup() { for s in "${SANDBOXES[@]}"; do chmod -R u+rwX "$s" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$s"; done; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# fresh <title>: a new empty sandbox (HOME = $SB/home, data directory = $DATA), cwd = the sandbox
fresh() {

  SB=$(cd "$t" && pwd -P) || exit 1

# show <file>: its scrubbed content, and whether it lacks a final newline
show() { scrub <"$1"; if [ -s "$1" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c 1 "$1")" ]; then echo; echo "(no newline at end)"; fi; }
not_root() { [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ] || { echo "(skipped: running as root)"; return 1; }; }
# snapfile <label> <file>: the state of one file
snapfile() {

# arg display: an empty or spaced argument is quoted

# The pty driver: argv = <out|both> <stderr file> <command...>. stdin is /dev/null, stdout (and stderr when `both`)

def end_of_call(s, k):
    depth, commas, m = 1, 0, k

            while s[m] != '"':

/// The kitty image of an icon: its embedded PNG, or the template tinted with its colour (made when it is sent).
pub(crate) fn kitty_image(icon: IconId) -> KittyImage {

        IconId::Png(index) => KittyPixels::Png(PNGS[index].1),
        IconId::Tinted(r, g, b) => KittyPixels::Rgba(tinted(r, g, b)),
    };
    KittyImage {
        id: icon.value(),
        src,
    }
}
